title: The production possibility frontier

title: Demand and supply shifting

title: Elastic and inelastic revenue

title: A negative externality
about: Negative externality|Marginal private cost (MPC)|Marginal social cost (MSC)
html: The market makes Qm, where demand meets the firm's own cost, MPC Add the pollution others pay for: MSC = MPC + external cost Society's best output Q* is where demand meets MSC Qm is more than Q*: over-production, a welfare loss. A tax can close it

title: The circular flow of income
about: Circular flow of income|Injections and withdrawals
html: Households spend at firms; firms pay wages, rent and profit back: the circular flow Withdrawals leak out of the flow: saving, taxes, imports Injections come in: investment, government spending, exports. More in than out, and income grows

title: How a rate rise works through
html: Monetary policy: the Bank of England raises the base rate Borrowing costs more and saving pays more, so spending falls Less demand, so prices rise more slowly: inflation falls towards the 2% target

title: √2 is irrational
html:
1Suppose √2 = a ÷ b, a fraction in lowest terms
2Square both sides: 2 = a² ÷ b², so a² = 2b²
3a² is 2 × something, so a² is even — and so a is even: a = 2k
4Then 2b² = (2k)² = 4k², so b² = 2k²: b is even too
5Both even means both share the factor 2 — not lowest terms. Contradiction.
6So the supposition is false: √2 is irrational ∎

title: Syllogisms in circles
html: All dogs are mammals, all mammals are animals: dogs must sit inside animals. Valid All cats are mammals, all dogs are mammals… so all dogs are cats? Dogs can sit inside cats or outside them: the conclusion is not forced. Invalid

title: A gallery of fallacies
html:
Straw man
A: We should have fewer cars in the town centre.
B: So you want to ban cars and close every shop in town?
It knocks down a weaker view that nobody put forward.
Ad hominem
A: This study shows sugar harms children’s teeth.
B: Why listen to him? He can’t even keep his garden tidy.
It attacks the person; the evidence stands or falls on its own.
False dilemma
A: Either we build the new road, or the town centre dies.
B: Isn’t there a third way, like a better bus service?
It offers two options as if they were the only ones.

title: Arguments for the existence of God
A chain of causes
html: This oak came from an acorn, which came from an oak… every effect has a cause Aquinas: the chain cannot go back for ever, so there is a first cause, itself uncaused Hume: why could the chain not be infinite? And why must a first cause be God?

title: Paley's watch
html: A stone on a heath: for all we know, it has always lain there A watch: its parts framed and put together for a purpose. It must have had a maker Paley: the eye is more intricate than any watch, so nature too has a designer Hume and Darwin: the world is as like a plant as a machine, and natural selection can build design

title: The problem of evil and theodicies
The trolley problem
html: A runaway trolley will kill five. A lever would send it onto a track with one person A utilitarian counts outcomes: switch, since one death is fewer than five A Kantian asks what you may do to a person: killing the one uses him merely as a means Same facts, two verdicts. Make it pushing a man off a bridge, and most people refuse

title: Ethics: virtue, natural law and situation ethics
Plato's cave
html: Chained since birth, the prisoners see only shadows, and take them for the real things One is freed and turns: the fire and the carried objects were casting the shadows He climbs out, dazzled, and sees the sun: for Plato, the Form of the Good

title: Doubting down to the cogito
html: Descartes doubts the senses: they have deceived him before He might be dreaming, so even waking life can be doubted An evil demon might deceive him even about arithmetic But doubting is thinking, so the doubter must exist: I think, therefore I am
